Subject: Burst seat blending: how discounts prorate across mixed SKUs?

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the quick demo yesterday. Procurement has a couple follow-ups before we finalize the SOW: namely how discounts and minimum floors apply when we mix reserved seats (committed GPU seat bundles) with variable per-token usage on top. We have a few specific asks — could you confirm by EOD if possible?

1) If we commit to 10 seats at a 25% committed-seat discount and then burst to 14 seats for a week, how does that 25% discount apply to the excess 4 seats? Is there an overage rate or does the committed discount only apply to the 10 committed seats?

2) We plan to also pay for per-token generation above a monthly token threshold. Do per-token discounts tier separately from seat discounts? If so, is there any rounding or minimum floor we should expect for small token increments (e.g., < 0.5k tokens)?

3) For long-context calls (we sent a sample payload >64k tokens during the trial), is there any context-length surcharge that interacts with per-token metering or the seat discount? For example, does the platform meter tokens differently for >32k contexts?

4) Request: please provide a simple sample invoice / line-item math using our projected numbers so our finance team can reconcile.

Appreciate the help — we need this to complete vendor approval.

Hi Renee — thanks, and great questions. Looping in Ben for commercial detail and Priyom for the billing math. We put together a short illustrative workbook and a draft proforma invoice (attached).

Quick answers up-front so procurement can move:
- Committed-seat discount applies only to the committed seats. Overage seats are billed at the burst/overage rate in the SOW; we can offer a stepped overage discount for predictable burst weeks (example in the attached sheet).
- Per-token charges and seat charges are billed as separate line items; discounts do not cascade from seats to tokens automatically. However, we can map a blended effective rate in the deal for negotiation (i.e., apply a per-token rebate as a contra line item).
- Context-length metering: tokens are the basis (including system/prompt tokens). Longer contexts do not incur a separate "surcharge" unless you use our extended context premium models; if you do, that model has a different per-token rate and may have a different rounding quantum.

Ben — can you confirm the overage step examples and the language we should propose for contract? Priyom — Ben noted you'd include the line-by-line math (rounding/minimums) in the workbook.

Next steps: Ben to confirm rates, Priyom to finalise sample invoice, Hannah to share contract language snippet for seat/overage discount.

Thanks — Hannah

Hi Renee — thanks for the clear asks. Below is a concise worked example using your numbers (we included the full sheet in the attachment). I'll keep this to concrete math so finance can follow.

Assumptions (monthly):
- Committed seats: 10 seats at list $6,000/seat/mo -> seat list total = $60,000
- Committed-seat discount: 25% -> committed-seat charge = $60,000 * (1 - 0.25) = $45,000
- Bursted seats (overage): 4 seats for 7 days (we bill overage proportionally by day)
  - Overageday rate = list seat rate * 1.0 (no committed discount) = $6,000/seat/mo pro-rated to 7/30 days -> per-seat overage = $6,000 * (7/30) = $1,400 
  - Total overage seats charge = 4 * $1,400 = $5,600
- Per-token usage above threshold: 2,400,000 tokens @ $0.0008/token (list) = $1,920
  - We offer a 10% per-token rebate if monthly token volume > 2M (deal negotiation) -> per-token after rebate = $1,728

Invoice line math (sample):
1) Seats (committed): $45,000 (10 seats at discounted net price)
2) Seat overage (burst): $5,600 (4 seats pro-rated, no committed discount)
3) Per-token (post-rebate): $1,728

Subtotal = $45,000 + $5,600 + $1,728 = $52,328
Tax/other = as applicable

Rounding and minimums:
- Token metering: billed at token granularity but aggregated monthly. We round token-based line items to the nearest whole token (no fractional-token billing). For monetary rounding, we round invoice line totals to cents using standard bankers rounding.
- Minimums: committed seats are guaranteed and invoice the committed net even if not used. There's no additional floor applied to per-token lines beyond any negotiated per-token minimum (we can define a per-token minimum in the SOW if you need a floor).

Context-length and long-history impacts:
- We meter all tokens that make up the request/response sequence. If you use our <extended-context> model (32k+ variants), the model's per-token list price is higher; the price multiplier is applied on the token line item. There is not a separate seat surcharge tied to context length.

Contract language suggestion (seat overage):
"Committed-seat discounts apply only to the number of seats specified in Section X. Any capacity used above the committed quantity in a billing period will be billed at the then-current overage rate set forth in the pricing schedule; overage charges will be prorated by day for partial-month bursts."

If helpful, we can propose a stepped overage discount for any sustained month where average daily seats exceed the committed seats by more than 20% (example in sheet).

Priyom — please confirm the rounding language in the invoice and I can fold this into the SOW.

Thanks,
Ben

If so, do you pro-rate the rebate mid-month or apply it on the subsequent month?

If you can add two short sentences to the contract language and update the sample invoice to reflect timezone/day-pro-ration and rebate-applied-next-month semantics, procurement can sign off.
